stories.kicker: The World · The Gulf of Oman
stories.headline: The Ship No One Will Claim, and the Coast That Joined No War
stories.dek: A sanctioned ghost-fleet tanker, abandoned since June with 800,000 barrels of Russian crude aboard, has become the Gulf's worst slick in years. The salvage stalled for a reason worth sitting with: the ship's insurer is under sanctions too.

stories.headline: The Chips Cross the Border — and Beijing Parks Them in Hong Kong
stories.dek: After a year of paper approvals and rented-cloud workarounds, physical H200s are landing in China. The licences come with a leash: most of the silicon must stay off the mainland, in a city that cannot power it at scale.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · Watchmaking — The Invitation
stories.headline: The Only Hobby Where You Break It On Purpose
stories.dek: Collectors buy the watch. This lot takes it apart, loses a spring into the carpet at two in the morning, and calls it Tuesday. An invitation to the fiddliest bench in the house — and to the craft the professionals are quietly leaving.

stories.headline: The Board Lights Up Again, Days Before the Rally
stories.dek: A dry spell over Sumatra and Kalimantan has pushed the haze watch back on — and this year the season was flagged red before it began. The reading is still moderate. The forecast is the worry.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Buy It Once — No. 4 · Watch Winders
stories.headline: The Machine That Rocks, or the Furniture That Glows
stories.dek: A category split down the middle: instrument-grade engineering on one side, velvet-lined theatre on the other. The honest question is not which winder to buy. It is whether your Grand Seiko wants one at all.

stories.headline: Bose Makes Its Best Headphones Cheaper
stories.dek: The standard QuietComfort — not the Ultra — gets Immersive Audio and, for the first time on this line, wired lossless over USB-C. At US$359, it is the clearest "you don't need the flagship" pitch Bose has made in years.

stories.headline: The Most Famous Deck on Earth, Dipped in Gold
stories.dek: Technics marks fifty-five years of the SL-1200 with a numbered anniversary edition in seven colours. It is the most collectable version of the deck ever made — and, underneath the gold, the same machine as a turntable costing three hundred dollars less.

stories.headline: A Dinosaur in the Cul-de-Sac, and the Critics Out-Liked the Crowd
stories.dek: The It Follows director trades arthouse dread for Amblin-scale spectacle. Most reviewers cheered; a vocal minority walked out cold — and, unusually, the professionals liked it more than the audience did.

stories.headline: Move Her, Don't Just Monitor Her — But Read the Fine Print
stories.dek: The largest cohort yet finds organised sport at eleven protects a child's later mental health. The catch a parent of a daughter should hear: the protective dose is roughly half as strong for girls — and it lands right as they start walking away.

stories.headline: The Thirty-Year Hit a Nineteen-Year High. Then the Treasury Bought It Back Down.
stories.dek: A fiscal-fear bear steepener took the long bond to levels last seen in 2007 — and Washington's own debt manager stepped between the market and the price. Market explanation, not advice.

stories.headline: The VO2 Max Curve Bends Further Than the Calendar Says
stories.dek: A study of lifelong multi-marathoners finds the age-related drop in cardiorespiratory fitness is far more trainable than the textbook decline assumes. And last month's strength "sweet spot" has grown a number worth pinning up: dementia.

stories.headline: October Is a Wall of Stadium Nights — Book Ahead of the Crush
The Country That Went Furthest Into Faith Is Buying It by the Livestream
stories.dek: As Thai Buddhism suffers its worst credibility crisis in a generation, Gen Z has not stopped believing. It has cut out the temple — routing its faith through a TikTok marketplace of livestreamed fortune-tellers, subscription horoscopes and amulet auctions.
